summary: A small Russian crew that launches Molniya drones on a fibre-optic cable. The drone ignores jammers and hits armour hard, but the crew carries only three and must work close to the target and to supply.

sections.title: Molniya drone
sections.how: Select the crew and left-click an enemy, or Ctrl + left-click the ground to send a drone at a spot.
sections.body: Each launch sends a fixed-wing drone at the target. The drone carries no gun: it flies there and detonates an anti-tank warhead, destroying itself. It is best against tanks and light vehicles; its small blast barely touches spread-out infantry, and it cannot attack aircraft. The crew launches only at short range, so it has to work near the front. Small arms and other weapons that can hit low flyers can shoot the drone down on the way.

sections.title: Reload drones
sections.how: Park the crew within five tiles of an own supply truck, supply center or barracks. No order is needed.
sections.body: The crew carries three drones, shown as pips over the selected squad. Every launch spends one. With none left the crew launches nothing, drops its attack order and waits; it can still be ordered to move. One drone comes back after a wait while the crew stays beside a supply source. Driving the truck away or walking out of range resets the wait. Bring the crew home or bring a truck forward before the next fight.

sections.title: Fibre link and jammers
sections.how: No order is needed: the fibre line cannot be cut by a jammer. Keep the crew alive until the drone lands.
sections.body: The Molniya is steered through a fibre-optic cable, not by radio. A Pole-21's circle does not drop it, scatter its aim or stop it. Only Russia fields a jammer, so in practice a Russian crew never meets a hostile one. The same fibre ties the drone to its crew: if the crew is killed while the drone is in the air, the drone falls harmlessly. Small arms, machine guns and other weapons that reach low flyers are the way to stop it.

sections.title: Dig trenches
sections.how: Select the crew, press Dig trench and left-click the ground. Drag to draw a line; Shift turns a single trench or keeps the button armed after a line.
sections.body: A crew digs a two-cell trench; more diggers finish faster. A finished trench halves the damage its infantry take, and a section with a roof protects the first two soldiers completely. Wheeled vehicles cannot cross it once it is half dug; tracked vehicles and infantry can.

sections.title: Fight from a trench
sections.how: Select the crew and left-click a finished trench, or press Garrison.
sections.body: Inside a trench the crew is protected: small arms and most fire only graze it, while high explosives and thermobaric shells wear the trench down and can destroy it. It still launches drones over the parapet at vehicles, and at point-blank it fights with a sidearm. A trench line lets the crew move from piece to piece toward the enemy. Press Unload to get out.

sections.title: Garrison buildings
sections.how: Select the crew and left-click a civilian building, or press Garrison.
sections.body: The crew takes cover inside and launches drones from the windows with more range. The building changes hands to your side while they hold it and returns to neutral when they leave. A wrecked building throws them out, and one that collapses can kill them.

sections.title: Heal at the barracks
sections.how: Select damaged crews and left-click your barracks.
sections.body: They walk in and heal for free while the barracks keeps training. A patient leaves on its own when whole. If the barracks is destroyed or sold, the patients are thrown out.

sections.title: Ride in vehicles
sections.how: Select one or more crews, then left-click your own BRDM-2 or BMP-2.
sections.body: They climb aboard and cannot be selected until they get out. A BRDM-2 has firing ports, so its passengers can fire from inside; a BMP-2 has none, so they ride protected but silent. If the BRDM-2 is destroyed its riders are killed, while a destroyed BMP-2 only hurts them. Select the loaded vehicle and press Unload to let them out.

sections.title: Repair bridges
sections.how: Select one or more soldiers and left-click a damaged or broken bridge.
sections.body: The soldiers walk to the bank and repair the bridge for free. Every worker adds a share, up to six; a dozer counts for three. A broken bridge opens again once it is repaired enough to carry traffic.

strong: Short-range ambushes from a trench or building
weak: Small arms and low-air defenses against the drone
Infantry spread out beyond the blast
Running out of drones away from supply
Losing the crew while a drone is in the air
tips: Keep the crew close: the Molniya only reaches short-range targets, so it has to work near the line.
Bring a supply truck forward or park the crew beside the barracks between sorties; three drones go quickly.
A jammer cannot stop the drone, so spend the charges on armour rather than hunting the Pole-21.
Aim at tanks and light vehicles; the small warhead wastes its blast on scattered infantry.
Put the crew in a trench or building: it launches from cover and is easier to keep alive.
Small arms are the real threat to the drone; keep it away from riflemen and machine guns.
